# rlibc-x

A minimal, educational Rust libc implementation for Linux x86_64.

## Goals

- **Educational** - Understand how Rust programs start, allocate memory, and interact with the kernel
- **Minimal binaries** - Explore whether simpler implementations can produce smaller binaries
- **Eventually transparent** - Long-term goal is to not require `#![no_std]` and `#![no_main]`

## Results

The rlibc-x1 + no_std approach produces a **1,480 byte** statically-linked executable:

```
$ cargo build -p ex-x1 --release && ls -la target/release/ex-x1
-rwxr-xr-x 2 wink users 1480 Jan 15 11:52 target/release/ex-x1

$ file target/release/ex-x1
ex-x1: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, stripped
```

This is achieved through:
- **`#![no_std]`** - No Rust standard library overhead
- **Direct syscalls** - `_start` → `_start_rust()` → `main()` → `exit()`
- **Bump allocator** - Simple `malloc`/`realloc` via `brk()`, `free()` is a no-op
- **`panic="abort"`** - No unwinding machinery
- **Aggressive optimization** - `opt-level='z'`, LTO, single codegen unit, stripped symbols

For comparison, rlibc-x2 (which supports `std`) produces ~41KB binaries.

See [apps/](apps/README.md#size-comparison) for the full size comparison across rlibc-x1, rlibc-x2, glibc, and musl.

## Workspace Structure

| Directory | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| [rlibc-x1/](rlibc-x1/) | `#![no_std]` runtime (~1.4 KB binaries) |
| [rlibc-x2/](rlibc-x2/) | `std`-compatible libc replacement (~41 KB binaries) |
| [apps/](apps/) | Example and comparison apps |
| [tools/](tools/) | Development tools (`is-libc-used`) |
| [xtask/](xtask/) | Project automation |

## Two Approaches

**rlibc-x1** (no_std): App uses `#![no_std]` and `#![no_main]`. Minimal, but requires explicit annotations.

**rlibc-x2** (std): App uses normal `fn main()` with Rust std. Replaces glibc while keeping std functionality.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Build and run
cargo xtask run hw-x1          # hello world with rlibc-x1
cargo xtask run hw-x2          # hello world with rlibc-x2

# Test
cargo xtask test               # run all tests
cargo xtask test -q            # quiet mode

# Build release
cargo xtask build -r           # release builds
```

For more information see [xtask/README.md](xtask/README.md)

## Verifying No libc Usage

The `is-libc-used` tool checks if a binary uses libc:

```bash
cargo run -p is-libc-used -- ./target/release/ex-x1
cargo run -p is-libc-used -- -v ./target/release/ex-x1  # verbose
```

All apps include libc usage tests that run with `cargo xtask test`.

## Status

This is an experimental/educational project. For production use, consider:

- [relibc](https://gitlab.redox-os.org/redox-os/relibc) - Redox OS's portable POSIX C library in Rust
- [c-ward](https://github.com/aspect-build/c-ward) - A libc implementation in Rust

## Origin

Started with this prompt for Claude Code:

> "I want to create a rust app that simply returns a number, something like `fn main -> i32 { 2 }`.
> I want to supply all code including the "standard libraries". I don't want the complication of
> code unwinding so panic="abort". So the minimum set of functions in lib.rs is _start, panic,
> exit, free, malloc, realloc, exit and probably a few others."

Initial versions created with Claude Code and ChatGPT. See [this ChatGPT conversation](https://chatgpt.com/share/695b4ae1-d84c-800c-8d09-34cff3de3b33) for the custom target approach.

## License

Licensed under either of

- Apache License, Version 2.0 ([LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE) or http://apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)
- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

### Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted
for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall
be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# Example and Comparison Apps

Binary size comparison across different runtimes.

## Size Comparison

| App | Runtime | Linking | Size | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-----:|-------------|
| ex-x1 | rlibc-x1 | static | 1.4 KB | Minimal exit-only (no_std + no_main) |
| ex-x2 | rlibc-x2 | static | 41.4 KB | Minimal exit-only (std with custom libc) |
| ex-glibc | glibc | dynamic | 283.7 KB | Minimal exit-only |
| ex-musl | musl | static | 372.6 KB | Minimal exit-only |
| hw-x1 | rlibc-x1 | static | 1.5 KB | Hello world |
| hw-x2 | rlibc-x2 | static | 45.8 KB | Hello world |
| hw-glibc | glibc | dynamic | 286.7 KB | Hello world |
| hw-musl | musl | static | 376.6 KB | Hello world |

## App Naming Convention

- **ex-** = exit-only (just returns an exit code)
- **hw-** = hello world (prints to stdout)
- **-x1** = uses rlibc-x1 (no_std)
- **-x2** = uses rlibc-x2 (std)
- **-glibc** = uses system glibc
- **-musl** = uses musl libc

## Building and Running

```bash
# Using xtask (recommended)
cargo xtask build ex-x1        # debug build
cargo xtask build ex-x1 -r     # release build
cargo xtask run hw-x1          # build and run

# Direct cargo commands
cargo build -p ex-x1 --release
cargo run -p hw-x1 --release

# glibc/musl targets (use aliases)
cargo b-glibc -p ex-glibc --release
cargo b-musl -p ex-musl --release
```

## Testing

Each app includes a test that verifies it doesn't use libc (for x1/x2 variants):

```bash
cargo xtask test ex-x1 hw-x1   # test specific apps
cargo xtask test               # test all
```

Excellent! Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the codebase. Let me create a final summary report.

## Comprehensive Codebase Exploration Report

### 1. Project Purpose

**rlibc-x** is an experimental, educational Rust implementation of libc for Linux x86_64. The project explores whether custom minimal libc implementations can produce significantly smaller binaries while maintaining Rust standard library compatibility. It achieves its smallest binaries at **1,480 bytes** for statically-linked executables (vs. 286KB+ for glibc/musl).

**Three core goals:**
- **Educational**: Understand Rust program initialization, memory allocation, and kernel interaction
- **Minimize binaries**: Explore smaller implementations through simplified approaches
- **Transparent replacement**: Eventually not require explicit `#![no_std]` and `#![no_main]` annotations

---

### 2. Overall Architecture and Structure

The project uses a **dual-implementation strategy** with a **workspace layout**:

```
rlibc-x/ (Workspace root)
├── rlibc-x1/           # Minimal no_std implementation (~1.4 KB binaries)
├── rlibc-x2/           # std-compatible replacement (~41 KB binaries)
├── apps/               # Example applications and comparisons
├── tools/              # Development utilities (is-libc-used, func-analysis)
├── xtask/              # Build automation and testing
└── Cargo.toml          # Workspace configuration
```

**Two Approaches:**

| Aspect | rlibc-x1 | rlibc-x2 |
|--------|----------|----------|
| Features | No std library | Full std support |
| Annotations | `#![no_std]` + `#![no_main]` | Normal `fn main()` |
| Binary size | 1.4-1.5 KB | 41-45 KB |
| Entry point | Direct `_start()` assembly | `__libc_start_main()` wrapper |
| Memory alloc | Bump allocator (brk syscall) | Bump allocator with memcpy/memset |

---

### 3. Main Modules and Responsibilities

#### **rlibc-x1** (`/rlibc-x1/src/lib.rs`) - 328 lines
Single-file, no_std minimal implementation:

- **Syscall layer**: `syscall0-6()` - Direct x86_64 assembly wrappers for Linux syscalls (rax, rdi, rsi, rdx, r10, r8, r9 registers)
- **Exit**: `exit(code)` - Process termination via SYS_EXIT (60)
- **I/O**: `read()`, `write()` - Direct syscall wrappers (SYS_READ=0, SYS_WRITE=1)
- **Memory management**:
  - `malloc()` - 16-byte aligned bump allocator using `brk()` syscall
  - `realloc()` - Allocate new block and copy data
  - `calloc()` - Allocate and zero-initialize
  - `free()` - No-op (bump allocator doesn't free)
- **Runtime**: 
  - `_start()` - Naked assembly entry point from kernel
  - `_start_rust()` - Initialize heap, call Rust main()
  - Panic handler: `panic()` - Exit with code 101
  - `rust_eh_personality()` - Unwinding stub

#### **rlibc-x2** (Modular design, 9 modules) - ~24 KB

Organized into focused modules providing glibc replacement:

1. **`syscall.rs`** - Raw x86_64 syscall wrappers (identical to rlibc-x1 but in separate module)
   - `syscall0-6()` inline functions
   - Syscall constants: SYS_READ, SYS_WRITE, SYS_BRK, SYS_EXIT, SYS_ARCH_PRCTL, SYS_POLL
   - arch_prctl commands: ARCH_SET_FS, ARCH_GET_FS

2. **`memory.rs`** - Memory allocation and manipulation
   - `malloc()`, `realloc()`, `calloc()`, `free()`, `posix_memalign()`
   - Memory ops: `memcpy()`, `memmove()`, `memset()`, `memcmp()`, `bcmp()`
   - **Critical detail**: Uses manual loops instead of core::ptr::* to avoid LLVM optimizing to libc calls
   - Heap state: HEAP_START, HEAP_END, HEAP_CURRENT (bump allocator)

3. **`process.rs`** - Process control and libc startup
   - `exit(code)` - Process termination
   - `abort()` - Abnormal termination (exit 134 = 128 + SIGABRT)
   - `__rust_start_panic()` - Rust panic entry point
   - `__libc_start_main()` - Core libc entry point called by _start:
     - Stores stack_end for overflow detection
     - Initializes heap and TLS
     - Sets up environ
     - Calls init/fini constructors/destructors
     - Calls user main(), then rtld_fini
   - `_start()` - Naked assembly kernel entry point

4. **`thread.rs`** - Thread-local storage and threading stubs
   - `init_tls()` - Set up TLS block via arch_prctl(ARCH_SET_FS)
   - pthread stubs: `pthread_self()`, `pthread_attr_*()`, `pthread_key_*()`
   - `__tls_get_addr()` - TLS access
   - `poll()` - File descriptor polling (needed by std)
   - `sysconf()` - System configuration (SC_PAGESIZE, SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)

5. **`environ.rs`** - Environment variables
   - `environ` - Global environment pointer
   - `init()` - Initialize environ at startup
   - `getenv()` - C-compatible environment variable lookup
   - Custom iterator for environ entries

6. **`io.rs`** - Basic I/O
   - `read()` - Read from file descriptor
   - `write()` - Write to file descriptor
   - `writev()` - Stub (TODO)

7. **`errno.rs`** - Error handling
   - Thread-local `ERRNO` static
   - `__errno_location()` - Get errno pointer
   - `strlen()` - String length
   - `__xpg_strerror_r()` - Error string (stub)

8. **`signal.rs`** - Signal handling stubs
   - `signal()`, `sigaction()`, `sigaltstack()`
   - `pause()` - Pause process

9. **`lib.rs`** - Module coordination
   - Re-exports key symbols (exit, environ)
   - Stubs for unimplemented functions (stub! macro) covering:
     - File system: close, dup, fcntl, fstat64, lseek64, open64, stat64, getcwd, readlink, realpath
     - Environment: getauxval
     - Memory mapping: mmap64, mprotect, munmap
     - Unwinding: _Unwind_* functions
     - Dynamic linking: dl_iterate_phdr
   - Generic `syscall()` wrapper for all 6-arg syscalls

### 6. Key Technical Insights

**Memory Management Strategy:**
- Simple bump allocator using Linux `brk()` syscall
- No tracking of individual allocations (free is no-op)
- 16-byte alignment for malloc
- Page-aligned growth (4KB pages) for efficiency
- Trade-off: Fast, small, but no memory reuse

**Direct Syscalls:**
- No libc overhead - direct x86_64 syscall instruction
- Manually specify register usage (rax=syscall #, rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8/r9=args)
- Requires naked assembly for _start to set up kernel ABI

**TLS/Thread-Local Storage:**
- Single TLS block allocated in malloc'd memory
- Self-pointer at end, FS register points to it
- Minimal implementation (64 bytes pre-allocated)

**Compatibility Layer (rlibc-x2):**
- Replaces glibc while keeping Rust std library
- Provides __libc_start_main to intercept std startup
- Careful avoidance of LLVM intrinsic optimizations (manual memory loops)

**Testing Strategy:**
- is-libc-used tool verifies no glibc/musl symbols in binary
- Size comparison apps benchmark across implementations
- Per-crate testing with result aggregation
